gen_risks.description: Implementing agencies (PPS, MoE, MoLEVSA) lack experience with World Bank procurement guidelines, creating risk of procurement delays and compliance failures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated, qualified procurement experts within PPS and MoLEVSA and provide intensive World Bank procurement training to agency staff.
gen_risks.evidence: most of the entities involved in project implementation, have no experience in implementing World Bank-funded projects and with Bank procurement

gen_risks.description: Disparate and severe NES caseworker caseloads (ranging from 200 to over 2,000 clients per worker) overload staff with administrative duties and impair labor placement quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt staff reallocations across branch offices, re-deploy administrative staff, and establish a new registry separating active jobseekers from inactive registered persons.
gen_risks.evidence: average caseload varies between around 200 to over 2,000 registered unemployed per case worker across branch offices

gen_risks.description: Financial Management and Control (FMC) frameworks are not systematically established across participating government entities, creating substantial residual fiduciary risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign dedicated financial management specialists in the PIU, maintain strict Project Operations Manual internal controls, and execute annual independent financial audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Financial Management and Control (FMC), as designed by the PIFC framework required in the EU accession process, is not widely established

gen_risks.description: Failure or delay in achieving Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) under Part A could lead to the withholding or forfeiture of loan reimbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an inter-ministerial Policy Planning, Monitoring, and Coordination Working Group to track DLI progress semi-annually and utilize partial DLI payment mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Part A reimburses 'Eligible Expenditure Programs' (EEPs...) conditioned on the achievement of 'Disbursement-Linked Indicators' (DLIs).

gen_risks.description: Institutional resistance and political inertia may delay the restructuring and consolidation of Ministry of Economy development agencies with overlapping mandates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formulate and formally endorse a clear, costed, time-bound strategic framework and action plan signed directly by the Minister of Economy.
gen_risks.evidence: agencies have overlapping mandates, little coordination between them, and unclear links with the broader economic policy goals.

gen_risks.description: Entrenched academic culture focused solely on research publications may cause resistance among R&D institutes to performance-based financing and commercialization reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct RDI self-assessments and international expert audits to collaboratively design performance-based management schemes supported by targeted technical assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: exists a very strong academic culture, fueled by an incentive system that places a clear premium on publications with little incentives for protection

gen_risks.description: Public research projects in Serbia are concentrated in basic sciences at low technology readiness levels, leading to high failure rates during commercialization attempts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy specialized Technology Transfer Facility service lines at the Innovation Fund to provide commercialization mentorship and transaction support.
gen_risks.evidence: most high quality projects hail from the basic sciences, are at early technology readiness levels, and far from market readiness.

gen_risks.description: Historically weak inter-ministerial policy coordination and non-evidence-based planning could impede cross-agency execution of competitiveness and jobs reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Institutionalize an inter-ministerial PPMC Working Group led by the Public Policy Secretariat with mandatory ministry-level KPI reporting frameworks.
gen_risks.evidence: According to the Bank’s 2015 Systematic Country Diagnostic, policy coordination is among the weakest points for Serbia.

gen_risks.description: High effective marginal tax rates and 100% benefit withdrawal rules heavily disincentivize social financial assistance beneficiaries from accepting formal low-wage jobs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a comprehensive study on tax-benefit disincentives and pilot a targeted in-work conditional cash transfer program for social assistance recipients.
gen_risks.evidence: social assistance benefit that is reduced by at least one dinar—often by much more—for every dinar earned formally.

gen_risks.description: Small-scale enterprise R&D matching grant sub-projects and technology transfer activities could generate Category B physical environmental impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage an Independent Environmental and Social Expert to screen all sub-grant proposals against the ESMF and require site-specific Environmental Management Plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Direct, physical environmental impacts could arise under Component 2 on Innovation, which includes DLIs supporting startups and enterprises

gen_risks.description: Complex clearance and review arrangements between line ministries and the Public Policy Secretariat may cause procurement processing delays for technical assistance contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Specify detailed approval timelines and procurement protocols within the Project Operations Manual and conduct close implementation supervision.
gen_risks.evidence: arrangements for clearance of evaluation reports by the PPS may lead to procurement delays due to consultation with the respective implementing institutions

gen_risks.description: Broader fiscal consolidation measures, civil service salary cuts, and hiring limits may constrain public agency operational capacity to execute labor market activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Optimize NES staff allocation toward frontline casework, apply statistical profiling to target ALMPs efficiently, and leverage donor technical assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: recent reduction in civil service salaries, the ongoing constraints in the civil service to hire new workers, and budget limitation in financing

gt_risks.description: Program success relies on continuous, engaged commitment from the Prime Minister, Deputy PM, Minister of Finance, Minister of Education/Science/Technological Development, Minister of Labor/Employment/Veterans/Social Affairs, and the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS); line ministries must sustain interest in policy coordination or the loan will not disburse. Risk is heightened by political instability, frequent historical changes in ministers/senior staff, and excessive concentration of decision-making at the top (per the Bank's Systematic Country Diagnostic).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strong communications with the public, private sector, civil society, and EU Delegation to maintain a broad-based reform coalition; Bank coordinates communications with the PM's office; periodic PPMC Working Group consultations with private sector/civil society; ongoing close consultation with the EU Delegation in Serbia.

gt_risks.description: Significant downside macroeconomic risks: lower-than-expected Eurozone recovery could hurt Serbia's exports, remittances, and capital flows (EU countries are its largest trading partners). Materializing fiscal risks (e.g. SOE subsidy reduction difficulties) or weakening growth/currency would require even greater fiscal consolidation in 2015-2016 to keep public debt sustainable; reduced exports/FDI or greater consolidation could dampen anticipated reform impact.
gt_risks.mitigation: Bank works closely with government and the IMF to keep SOE/public-utility reform on track and ensure it generates required fiscal savings.

gt_risks.description: Project works across three ministries (MoE plus development agencies, MoESTD, MoLEVSA) plus the PPS, creating implementation complexity for both government and Bank. Achieving the DLIs requires substantial external technical assistance, but Bank supervision resources are limited and the government is reluctant to borrow for TA (would rather minimize loan-funded TA or substitute other donor resources), risking inadequate TA resourcing.
gt_risks.mitigation: Team seeks complementary resources (e.g. CIIP Trust Fund) and leverages work from other WBG projects; collaborates with other donors such as the EU and USAID.

gt_risks.description: Overall coordination sits with the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS), created only in spring 2014 under the new government; as a new institution it lacks capacity and a full set of official administrative procedures for cross-ministry policy coordination. Substantial risk to both project implementation (fiduciary/safeguards requirements, cross-ministry results reporting) and coordination of the inter-ministerial PPMC Working Group.
gt_risks.mitigation: PPS expected to hire additional personnel for fiduciary requirements and project coordination; Bank provides TA through the CIIP trust fund to strengthen PPS capacity.

gt_risks.description: PPS currently has no fiduciary experience managing Bank projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Build capacity by establishing a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within the PPS responsible for implementation, adequately staffing its fiduciary functions.

gt_risks.description: Reforms create both winners and losers, and losers are often more visible and organized at the time of reform (e.g. beneficiaries of MoE incentives/subsidies, National Employment Service case-workers, researchers at research institutes slated for restructuring).
gt_risks.mitigation: Government to clearly communicate reform objectives, expected outcomes, and benefits throughout the process.
